speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me what specific feeding difficulties your 8-month-old is experiencing, such as vomiting or refusal to eat? Also, how long has the abdominal distension been present?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby passed any stool recently, and is there any blood or mucus present in their diaper? I also need to know if they have had any episodes of vomiting, and if so, whether it was green or bilious.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas since the feeding difficulties began, and do you notice any palpable masses when you gently feel the abdomen? Also, could you describe the color of the baby's stool during the last successful bowel movement?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas at all since the swelling started, and is the stool tarry or bloody when it does come? I also need to check if the vomiting has been green or bilious, as that would indicate a blockage. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Test (WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets): Normal. Abdominal X-Ray Findings: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction. Barium Enema Findings: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease. Vital Signs: Heart Rate 120 bpm, Respiratory Rate 30 breaths/min, Temperature 36.8°C, Blood Pressure Normal for age. Physical Exam: Abdominal distension, tympanitic sound in left lower quadrant, soft but distended abdomen with crying intensifying on palpation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and the barium enema findings showing a transition zone strongly suggests Hirschsprung disease. I will confirm this with a rectal biopsy to assess the absence of ganglion cells. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease.
